title: Most frequent value in a rolling window
prompt: Given an integer array numbers and a window size k (1 <= k <= numbers.length), return the most frequent value in each consecutive window of k elements. If values tie, choose the smaller value. For numbers = [2, 1, 2, 3, 3] and k = 3, return [2, 1, 3]. Explain your approach before implementing it, and discuss the time and space costs.
followUps: How does your solution break frequency ties?
Which tests would expose mistakes when a value leaves the window?
What changes if k is almost as large as the input?

twist.prompt: The input is now an unbounded stream, and you may retain only the current window plus its index structures. Explain how you would adapt your solution.

hints: Start by solving one window correctly before reusing work.
Track counts as one value leaves and one arrives.
Consider how to find the best count and smallest tied value without sorting the entire window each time.
